Avery / Daniel —

I ran three representative scenarios in the attached spreadsheet (same file Ben referenced) and pulled out token/sec and p95 latency estimates assuming your workload profile:

Workload summary (from your docs):
- Avg response size: 450 tokens
- 75% short interactions (<= 600 tokens), 25% long-form (1200-1800 tokens)
- Peak concurrent requests (observed): 38
- KV-cache hit estimate: 22% (prefix-heavy dialogs)

Server/Model assumptions:
- Model baseline: mix-large-v1 (approx. 16B), FP16 and int8 quantized variants tested
- NVIDIA A100 80GB (current baseline) and H100 80GB (optional premium)
- Continuous batching enabled; conservative batch sizing for latency targets

Key numbers (per-GPU sustained tokens/sec at 95th percentile, conservative tuning):
- A100 / FP16: 5,200 tok/s (p95 latency ~1.9s for 450-token responses in single-GPU allocations)
- A100 / int8-quant: 7,800 tok/s (p95 ~1.2s for 450-token responses; quantization quality tested on your sample prompts)
- H100 / FP16: 8,500 tok/s (p95 ~1.1s)
- H100 / int8-quant: 12,300 tok/s (p95 ~0.7s)

Mapping to your target SLOs and headroom:
- If you want p95 <= 1.2s for 95% of traffic, int8 on A100 requires ~3.2 GPUs for steady-state token demand at peak (we recommend rounding up to a 4-GPU slab). That gives ~22% headroom for bursty long-form requests.
- If you want p95 <= 0.9s, H100 int8 is the practical option: ~2 GPUs steady-state, 3 GPUs slab to absorb spikes and canary rollouts.

Example calculation (conservative):
- Peak token arrival rate = peak concurrent * avg tokens per request / avg request duration. To be conservative, treat long-form as blocking the GPU for the full generation window. Using measured tails, we project an effective peak token/sec of ~23,000 tok/s.
- A100 int8 capacity per GPU = 7,800 tok/s -> 23,000 / 7,800 = 2.95 -> round to 4 GPUs.

Operational considerations and tradeoffs:
- Cache hit rate materially reduces steady-state tokens/sec; a 10% increase in KV cache hits reduces needed GPUs by ~0.3 at peak for A100-int8.
- Batching increases throughput but can harm p95 for interactive flows; our config uses latency-aware batching with a 40ms timer cap.
- Quantization (int8) saved ~50% compute vs FP16 in our tests but you should validate on a representative eval set for quality regressions. We ran your 120 prompt set and saw negligible quality delta on the int8 path for the majority of dialogs.

Attachments in the spreadsheet: per-GPU tok/s sensitivity, per-request p95 mapping, recommended slab sizes for a pilot (2-week canary):
- Pilot A (cost-prioritized): 4 x A100-int8 slab, 15% burst buffer (recommended commit band: 4-6 GPUs)
- Pilot B (latency-prioritized): 3 x H100-int8 slab with 30% burst buffer (commit band 3-5 GPUs)

I'll call out tolerances in the spreadsheet and included a simple ops playbook for fallbacks (model downgrade to smaller variant, region failover, automatic canary rollback on p95 regressions).

Let me know which pilot we should price and I'll ask Marissa to prepare the quote and provisional commit.

Karthik Iyer
